cultural.vision_reason: The image shows a traditional Hawaiian composite bone fishhook (makau) with fibre lashings and an olonā line, a well-documented Native Hawaiian fishing implement, matching the claimed ethnicity.

physical.title: fish-hook (makau)
physical.summary:
Composite makau (fish-hook) made of bone, and attached to an aho (line) made of thick twisted fibre, coiled into a bundle. 
The hook is made of two pieces of bone respectively forming a shank and a point, each indented and having a knob in the lower section. Both parts are tied together with thin fibre (possibly olonā), which is coiled over a wooden wedge used on one side of the hook as a tightener.
The shank is straight, with a knob in the upper section, around which coarse fibre is coiled to form a ka'a (snood) connecting to hook to the line. 
The point is slightly curved in, and has an inner barb.
The number "51" is handwritten onto the shank, in black ink.
